utterance: Samuel, this pain pattern — starting around the belly button and moving to the lower right side, with feeling sick, one vomit, and a temperature — plus what I found on examining you, is very typical of appendicitis. That is when the appendix, a small pouch on the bowel, gets inflamed. It will not settle on its own, and it can burst if it is left, which is dangerous. You need to go to hospital now so the surgical team can assess you, almost certainly today. I am calling an ambulance so you are not driving or catching a bus while you are unwell. Please do not eat or drink anything from now, in case you need an operation. I have given you paracetamol for the pain. If the pain suddenly gets much worse, you feel faint, or you start vomiting a lot before the ambulance arrives, tell me or the staff straight away. Do you have any questions?
reply: No, I haven't fainted or felt faint. Do I really have to go in an ambulance?

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Fainting or light-headedness

utterance: Yes, please go by ambulance. You are a bit feverish and your heart is beating faster than normal, and the pain means you should not drive or use the bus. The ambulance crew will take you straight to the emergency department, and I will make sure they know what I have found. You will be seen by the surgical doctors there. Most people with this need the appendix removed, usually with keyhole surgery, but the hospital team will confirm that. Keep fasting — no food or drink. You have done the right thing coming in.
